scene.title: The Hollow Parish
scene.description: A drowned village that should not be on any map: an empty church that rings, pilgrims who never left, and a warden counting souls.
scene.gm_directive: You are the Game Master of a slow folk horror. Emphasize wrongness in small doses: too-quiet animals, too-polite villagers, water where it should not be. Never explain the horror outright.

clocks.name: The Rising Water
clocks.description: Black water climbs the church steps
clocks.finisher: The parish drowns: only rooftops and the belfry remain above black water.

clocks.name: The Empty Belfry
clocks.description: The bell rings with no one in the tower
clocks.finisher: The thirteenth ringing: every door in the village opens at once.

clocks.name: The Warden's Count
clocks.description: The warden is counting the living
clocks.finisher: The count is complete: the parish claims one more soul — the hero, unless the count is broken.

quests.title: Who Rings the Bell
quests.description: Climb the belfry and learn what rings the bell — then stop it.

objectives.text: Earn the warden's trust — or pick the lock

quests.title: The Pilgrims Who Stayed
quests.description: Discover why the pilgrims never left the parish.

quests.title: A Road Out
quests.description: Find the old pilgrim road before the water closes it.

npcs.name: Warden Hobb
npcs.personality: Hospitable the way a trap is hospitable
npcs.position: On the church porch, counting on their fingers

npcs.name: Widow Lark
npcs.personality: Kind-eyed, evasive, mends the same net nightly

npcs.name: Tam
npcs.personality: Too calm, too polite, hums drowned hymns
notes: Knows the bell schedule by heart

npcs.name: Pilgrim Sorrow
npcs.personality: Exhausted, lucid in flashes, begs to be believed
notes: Arrived a week ago; has not slept since

factions.name: The Parish
factions.description: Villagers who smile a fraction too long
factions.ideology: Devout appeasement of the sea and strict adherence to the drowned registry.

factions.name: The Road Folk
factions.ideology: Transient survival, scavenging forgotten goods, and staying mobile on the road.

factions.name: The Drowned
factions.ideology: Inescapable reclamation of the land by the cold abyss.

abilities.name: Blessed Oil
abilities.description: Consecrated lantern oil burns true things brighter.
abilities.effect: Reveals what hides in a room

abilities.name: Held Breath
abilities.description: Go still, go silent, go unnoticed.

abilities.name: Last Rite
abilities.description: Words that lay things to rest — if said in time.

scene.world_context: The parish is not on any reliable map: roads bend around it, letters from it arrive damp. The church stands empty yet the bell rings; the pilgrims came for one night years ago and never left; Warden Hobb counts souls the way others count sheep.
scene.narrator_style: Quiet dreadful prose in the present tense

location_map.name: Mud Lane
location_map.description: A drowned lane of sagging houses and too-polite windows.

location_map.name: The Drowned Church
location_map.description: An empty nave ankle-deep in black water; the stair to the belfry.

location_map.name: The Pilgrim Inn
location_map.description: Warmth, stew, and Widow Lark's unblinking kindness.

location_map.name: The Cellar Chapel
location_map.description: A candle-crowded cellar where the parish keeps its drowned.

facts.value: The church bell rings though the church stands empty
The pilgrims came for one night and never left

beats.text: Take lodging and feel out what is wrong here

beats.condition: when quest "The Pilgrims Who Stayed" active

beats.text: Climb to the ringer before the thirteenth ringing
beats.condition: when quest "Who Rings the Bell" active

beats.text: Leave by the pilgrim road — or join the count

scene.opening_narration: Drizzle threads Mud Lane. Every window holds a face, every face smiles a heartbeat too long, and from the drowned church comes the bell — rung by no hands you can see.
scene.first_message: Hobb: "A guest! The parish loves guests. Supper's hot, the beds are dry — and do count the bells with us tonight."
